Chapter 9: Mentorship, Giving Back, and Lifting Others
As your career grows and your dreams start to take shape, you might find yourself wondering—how can you help others along the way?
Think about it—so many of us reach our goals because someone believed in us or gave us a chance when we needed it most.
The idea of paying it forward—of opening doors for someone else—becomes more than just a nice thought. It feels like both a responsibility and a privilege.
There’s a story that comes to mind. Picture a woman looking back at her journey. She remembers the mentors who were there for her—like the teacher who encouraged her writing, the colleague who spoke up for her in a meeting, or the friend who listened when self-doubt crept in.
Their support didn’t just help her succeed—it made all the difference. Now, she’s the one in a position to help others, and she’s asking herself, “How can I do this well?”
Here’s the thing about mentorship: it’s not always about formal programs or big gestures. Sometimes, it’s as simple as a quiet word of encouragement, sharing a helpful resource, or connecting someone with the right person.
Other times, it means being real about the tough stuff—the setbacks, the rejections, those scary moments when things don’t go as planned.
Most of us don’t realize just how much a single act of kindness can shift the entire course of someone’s life.
Giving back isn’t only about helping others. It also keeps you grounded, reminding you why you started out in the first place. When you reach out and support someone, you remember that no one truly succeeds alone. We all stand on the shoulders of those who came before us.
And here’s something you might not expect—the more you give, the more you get back. You’ll find new perspectives, fresh energy, and a sense of purpose that goes way beyond personal achievements.
Over time, you realize that lifting others up doesn’t take away from your own success. In fact, it multiplies it. There’s room enough for everyone’s dreams in this world.
So, what really matters in the end? It’s not the awards or the accolades. It’s the lives you touch, the doors you open, and the paths you help make a little easier for those who follow.
That’s the kind of legacy that truly lasts.
